facts.text: Stage codes identify how far a standard has progressed from first draft to published text and whether published text is about to change.
facts.quote: Stage codes are the labels that tell you how far a standard has traveled from first draft to published text, and whether the published text is about to change.

facts.text: ISO/IEC CD TS 22440 on AI and functional safety, a joint ISO and IEC document, was at Committee Draft stage in 2026; the booklet therefore expects no publication before 2027 or 2028.
facts.quote: ISO/IEC CD TS 22440 on artificial intelligence (AI) and functional safety, a joint document with the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), was there in 2026, which is why the booklet expects no publication before 2027 or 2028

facts.text: The booklet reviewed the 2022 Draft International Standard of ISO 21815-3 rather than published text and warns that the final edition may differ.
facts.quote: the booklet reviewed the 2022 DIS of ISO 21815-3, not the published text, and warns the final edition may differ

facts.text: ISO 21815-4 passed its Final Draft International Standard ballot on 28 May 2026.
ISO/PRF 21815-5 was at Proof stage 50.20, meaning typeset text awaiting printing, in September 2026.
facts.quote: A Proof (PRF) is the typeset text awaiting printing, stage 50.20; ISO/PRF 21815-5 was there in September 2026.

facts.text: All five parts of ISO 19014 reached 'under publication' stage 60.00 in August 2026 for publication in October 2026; this stage means the vote is won and the text is being prepared, not yet a published standard.
facts.quote: "Under publication" is stage 60.00: the vote is won and the text is being prepared; all five parts of ISO 19014 reached it in August 2026 for publication in October 2026

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2 and ISO/TS 19014-5:2021 are Technical Specifications rather than full standards; a Technical Specification is published when a committee agrees on content but not yet on a full standard.
facts.quote: A Technical Specification (TS) is published when a committee agrees on content but not yet on a full standard; ISO/TS 21815-2 and ISO/TS 19014-5:2021 are examples

facts.text: ISO/TS 19014-5:2021 is being promoted to a full standard in October 2026.
facts.quote: the latter is being promoted to a full standard in October 2026

facts.text: ISO/PAS 8800 and draft ISO/PAS 34506 are Publicly Available Specifications, not full standards; the passage describes PAS publication as faster than Technical Specification publication.
facts.quote: A Publicly Available Specification (PAS) is faster still; ISO/PAS 8800 and the draft ISO/PAS 34506 are examples

facts.text: ISO/IEC TR 5469:2024 provides informative guidance on AI and functional safety, not requirements; Technical Reports are not full standards.
facts.quote: A Technical Report (TR) is informative guidance with no requirements; ISO/IEC TR 5469:2024 is "guidance on AI and functional safety, not a requirements document"

facts.text: The booklet marks ISO 19014, ISO 13849-2 and ISO 3691-4 as 'under revision', meaning the published edition remains in force while a replacement is in preparation.
facts.quote: "Under revision" means a published edition is in force but its replacement is in the pipeline; the booklet marks ISO 19014, ISO 13849-2 and ISO 3691-4 this way

facts.text: ISO 16001:2017 was confirmed in 2023, meaning a review found no need to change the standard.
facts.quote: "Confirmed" means a review found no need to change (ISO 16001:2017, confirmed 2023).

facts.text: The booklet's evidence labels '(draft)', '(under publication)' and '(under revision)' are based on standard stage codes.
facts.quote: The booklet's evidence labels "(draft)", "(under publication)" and "(under revision)" rest on these codes

facts.text: ISO 19014 Parts 1 to 5, ISO 21815-4 and ISO 21815-5 all change in October and November 2026, a few months before the design freeze; the program plan therefore needs a standards watch and a re-baselining step.
facts.quote: ISO 19014 Parts 1 to 5, ISO 21815-4 and ISO 21815-5 all change in October and November 2026, a few months before the design freeze, so the plan needs a standards watch and a re-baselining step
